anyOf.description:
A content item plus a page of its versions (download).

``versions`` is a ``PublicPage`` envelope (not a bare list). Default window
is newest-first with ``limit``/``offset`` on the GET; use ``latest_only`` /
``version`` to pin without paging the full history.

failed_draft_archived_at.description: Archived after 30 days with no saved version. Restore this item by ID to list it again.
failed_draft_archived_at.title: Failed Draft Archived At

status.description:
Status of a background job.

Terminal states: ``completed``, ``completed_with_errors``, ``failed``,
``cancelled``. Active (in-progress) states: ``queued``, ``running``.

``awaiting_review`` is a third class: not terminal (work may resume after a
human action) and not active (no automatic progress is being made). Pollers
should treat it as stop-and-review rather than keep waiting for a terminal
status. It is intentionally in neither ``is_terminal`` nor ``is_active``.
status.title: JobStatus

PublicContentVersionSummary

items.description:
One generator-declared sentence→URL attribution (per-assertion provenance).

Captured at generation time from the inline-linked body before rendering,
so it survives output modes that strip the links from the shipped
markdown. On a v1 version ``sentence`` is the surface text with markdown
link syntax reduced to labels and whitespace collapsed — the same
normalization the publish-time gate applies, so a gate can match body
citations to this receipt by exact string comparison. On a v2 article
version ``sentence`` is the sentence exactly as it appears in
``markdown_body`` (list, quote and heading markers dropped; inline links
kept on an ``inline_only`` body; never re-spaced), so it is a substring of
the published body. ``sentence_index`` is the 0-based ordinal of the
sentence span within the body; ``marker`` mirrors the first-appearance
citation marker of ``sources``.

anyOf.description: Who supplied a cited source of a v2 article (public ``origin``).
anyOf.title: ArticleSourceOrigin

items.title: PublicAssertionProvenance

items.description:
One regulated-content policy finding on a content version.

Present when the org configures regulated industries and the detail
request includes ``?include=compliance``. ``kind`` is a stable enum
(``unsourced_figure``, ``advice_tone``, ``off_brand_promotion``,
``missing_disclaimer``) so clients can branch without parsing
``message``. ``excerpt`` is the offending body span for text findings,
or null for structural findings such as ``missing_disclaimer``.

kind.description:
Deterministic regulated-content policy finding kinds.

Returned on public content reads with ``?include=compliance``. Stable
machine-readable values for branching on compliance findings.

``MISSING_DISCLAIMER`` marks a still-missing per-industry regulated
disclaimer; generation adds the canonical footer so a clean shipped draft
clears it.
kind.title: RegulatedPolicyFindingKind

anyOf.description: Opt-in quality signals projected from a version's persisted metadata. Every field is nullable/empty by default so a partial or absent metadata blob never breaks the contract. Populated only when the detail request asks for it (``GET /content/{id}?include=scoring``); otherwise the version's ``scoring`` stays ``None``.

items.description: One research source actually cited in a generated article's final body. Projected from the version's persisted ``used_sources`` metadata (captured at generation time, link-based). ``marker`` is the 1-indexed first-appearance ordinal, so an integrator can line these up with inline citation order.

anyOf.description: Who supplied a cited source of a v2 article (public ``origin``).
anyOf.title: ArticleSourceOrigin

origin.description: research: found by platform research. supplied: only facts you supplied cite this URL (its page was fetched and checked). null: unknown, for a v2 version saved before supplied-fact provenance was recorded on it whose content kit has since changed.

items.title: PublicArticleSource

items.description:
A fact you supplied with no source URL, as given to the writer.

It carries no link in the body, so it is listed here rather than in
``sources`` or ``assertion_provenance``. Recorded on the version when it
is written, so later kit changes do not alter it. ``[]`` for a v1
version; the version's list is ``null`` when unknown (a v2 version saved
before this was recorded whose content kit has since changed).
items.title: PublicSuppliedFact
